requirements.description: Locked Python toolchain, minimal ASGI runtime and local infrastructure are reproducible.
requirements.title: Deterministic platform foundation

requirements.title: Security automation baseline

requirements.description: Requirements, commits, branches, decisions and evidence remain auditable in Git.
requirements.title: Traceable engineering changes

requirements.description: The minimal runtime emits structured logs and provides health and version endpoints.
requirements.title: Structured runtime visibility

requirements.description: The runtime handles process signals cleanly and dependencies expose health checks.
requirements.title: Graceful runtime lifecycle

requirements.description: A production application factory establishes permanent backend boundaries: modular structure, runtime lifecycle, service metadata, dependency injection and shared platform primitives with no import-time external connections.
requirements.title: Production backend core boundaries

requirements.description: Phase start, closure, next-phase selection and the execution lock work generically for every registry phase with no hardcoded phase identifiers.
requirements.title: Generic engineering lifecycle continuation

requirements.description: CI and developer tooling validate any feat/fix/release phase from repository state without workflow edits, on one deliberate Python baseline consistent across every declaration.
requirements.title: Phase-neutral CI and unified toolchain

requirements.description: Strongly typed, environment-aware configuration with secret redaction that fails fast on missing or unsafe production values.
requirements.title: Validated runtime configuration

requirements.description: A production application factory serves a versioned /api/v1 surface with deterministic OpenAPI and preserved P00 compatibility endpoints.
requirements.title: Versioned production API foundation

requirements.description: All errors are normalized to an RFC 9457 Problem Details contract with stable NXS codes and no stack traces or internal identifiers exposed.
requirements.title: Stable API error contract

requirements.description: Every request carries an isolated request id and correlation id using contextvars that never leak between concurrent tasks.
requirements.title: Request and correlation context isolation

requirements.description: Production logging emits structured JSON with severity, service metadata and request correlation, and redacts secrets, credentials and sensitive headers.
requirements.title: Structured correlated logging

requirements.description: A vendor-neutral OpenTelemetry-ready boundary propagates trace context and correlates traces with logs in configurable no-op, local or export modes.
requirements.title: Telemetry instrumentation boundary

requirements.description: Separate liveness and readiness semantics with a typed dependency health model that degrades and recovers without process restart and never leaks credentials.
requirements.title: Liveness and readiness subsystem

requirements.description: Async pooled PostgreSQL engine and session factory with bounded timeouts, safe transaction primitives, health probe and graceful disposal, with no import-time connections.
requirements.title: PostgreSQL connectivity foundation

requirements.description: A canonical global user identity model with immutable server-generated UUIDv7 user_id, lifecycle status, normalized email identity, verified/unverified email state and no tenant trust from request bodies or arbitrary headers; tenant association is resolved only through authenticated membership.
requirements.title: User identity core

requirements.description: A secure user-organization membership boundary with status lifecycle, unique constraints preventing duplicate active membership ambiguity, safely scoped lookup, no cross-organization enumeration and no privilege inheritance between organizations.
requirements.title: Organization membership boundary

requirements.description: Argon2id password credentials with per-password salt through the library primitive, no custom or reversible storage, secure verification, credential versioning seam, length and normalization rules, protection against pathological hashing inputs and no password material in logs, errors or traces.
requirements.title: Password credentials

requirements.description: Short-lived access tokens with rotation-capable server-side refresh sessions, revocation and reuse detection, explicit issuer and audience validation, strict algorithm allowlist, exp/iat/nbf validation, key identifier support, bounded clock skew, no algorithm confusion and fail-closed malformed claims.
requirements.title: Token and session architecture

requirements.description: A provider-independent signing and verification key abstraction with key identifier rotation support, verification of old valid tokens during controlled rotation, a future external KMS/HSM seam, private key material never returned or logged, and hardened environments failing closed on insecure development key configuration.
requirements.title: Signing key management

requirements.description: Foundational organization-scoped role-based access control with stable permission identifiers, organization-scoped role assignments, a deny-by-default authorization service boundary, explicit permission checks, least privilege, no implicit admin from email or domain and no cross-tenant role leakage.
requirements.title: Organization-scoped RBAC

requirements.description: The production TenantContextResolver derives organization_id only from authenticated and authorized identity and membership context, never from arbitrary headers, request bodies, global fallback or unauthorized membership switching; proven by adversarial tests.
requirements.title: Authenticated tenant resolution

requirements.description: A minimal login, refresh, logout/revoke and session/identity API with generic authentication failure responses, stable error codes, no user enumeration, no password hashes, signing secrets or refresh tokens in responses or logs.
requirements.title: Authentication API surface

requirements.description: A bounded authentication abuse-control layer with failed-attempt throttling, no unbounded in-memory-only production security primitive, user/IP-aware keys where safe, deterministic tests and safe fallback behavior.
requirements.title: Authentication abuse control

requirements.description: Async Valkey client behind an internal abstraction with bounded connect and operation timeouts, health probe, lifecycle management and redacted URLs.
requirements.title: Valkey connectivity foundation

requirements.description: Async NATS connection manager with bounded connect timeout, reconnect policy, lifecycle callbacks, JetStream capability detection, health state and graceful drain.
requirements.title: NATS and JetStream connectivity foundation

requirements.description: Alembic is configured from validated database settings with an async-capable path, naming convention, deterministic execution and CI migration validation, committing no credentials.
requirements.title: Database migration framework

requirements.description: No Organization can read, write, mutate, cache, execute against or inherit another Organization's context — enforced in PostgreSQL by forced Row-Level Security and a non-bypass runtime role, not by application WHERE clauses — across data and compute, under raw SQL, connection-pool reuse, concurrency, rollback and spoofed identifiers.
requirements.title: Strict tenant isolation

requirements.description: A typed, immutable TenantContext resolved only from a trusted resolver boundary propagates organization_id through contextvars without leaking between concurrent async tasks and remains serializable for future cross-process work.
requirements.title: Trusted tenant context and propagation

requirements.description: Every tenant-scoped table has RLS ENABLED and FORCED with USING and WITH CHECK policies bound to the transaction-local organization_id; a missing tenant context yields zero visibility, never a global fallback.
requirements.title: PostgreSQL Row-Level Security enforcement

requirements.description: A first-class tenant unit-of-work sets the transaction-local tenant context, so pooled connection reuse across commit, rollback and exception paths cannot leak one Organization's scope into another's transaction.
requirements.title: Tenant-safe pooled database transactions

requirements.description: A deterministic namespace primitive prefixes every tenant-scoped resource name with organization_id (cache keys, locks, storage prefixes, job identity) with no implicit global fallback and bounded, safely encoded identifiers.
requirements.title: Tenant namespace isolation for compute and resources

requirements.description: The Organization aggregate — server-generated immutable UUIDv7 identity, normalized reserved-safe organization_key, validated profile fields, timezone-aware timestamps and optimistic-concurrency version — is persisted through the first real domain migration.
requirements.title: Organization core domain identity and persistence

requirements.description: Organization status transitions (PROVISIONING, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, ARCHIVED) are an explicit state machine enforced by the domain service; invalid transitions and operations on non-active Organizations return stable NXS errors and there is no hard delete through runtime repositories.
requirements.title: Organization lifecycle state machine

requirements.description: The application runtime connects to PostgreSQL as a role that is not superuser and cannot bypass RLS (NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS, no schema ownership of tenant tables, least DML); a separate migration role owns schema changes; staging and production fail closed if the runtime role can bypass tenancy.
requirements.title: Non-bypass tenant database runtime role

requirements.description: The backend and its production container build for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 with no architecture-specific committed binaries, gated in CI, ahead of the ARM64 NXS LAB environment.
requirements.title: AMD64 and ARM64 backend and container compatibility

requirements.description: Organizations are customer-facing tenants with automated, idempotent provisioning.
requirements.title: Organization provisioning

requirements.title: Dynamic organization dashboards

requirements.description: Security-sensitive tenant, human and AI actions produce tamper-evident auditable records.
requirements.title: Immutable platform audit

requirements.description: Metrics, traces, logs, SLOs and correlation span cells, channels and tenant operations.
requirements.title: End-to-end observability

requirements.description: The platform tolerates dependency and cell failures with tested degradation and recovery.
requirements.title: Failure resilience

requirements.description: Encrypted backups and regularly tested restores meet declared recovery objectives.
requirements.title: Backup and restore

requirements.description: One immutable, versioned event envelope with globally unique UUIDv7 event_id, UTC occurred_at, stable namespaced event_type, explicit event_version, trusted organization_id or an explicitly classified global scope, aggregate identity, correlation and causation identifiers, producer identity and a strongly typed payload; plus a deterministic NATS subject builder and parser that rejects malformed, injection-like or secret-bearing subjects and controls wildcards.
requirements.title: Canonical event envelope and subject taxonomy

requirements.description: A PostgreSQL transactional outbox so a business mutation and its event intent commit atomically in the same database transaction; no event is ever emitted from uncommitted state and no row is marked published before JetStream confirms the publication. Tenant-owned outbox rows follow forced Row-Level Security and the runtime role holds no unrestricted DELETE.
requirements.title: Transactional outbox for atomic state and event intent

requirements.description: A JetStream publisher that extends the P01 messaging boundary, checks the publish acknowledgement under a bounded timeout, classifies transient versus permanent failure, uses event_id as the JetStream message identity for broker-side deduplication, never silently falls back to core NATS for durable business events, and fails closed in hardened environments when required durability is unavailable.
requirements.title: Reliable JetStream publisher with deterministic semantics

requirements.description: A reusable durable consumer abstraction with a stable consumer identity, an explicit acknowledgement policy, bounded ack-wait, a bounded handler timeout, controlled concurrency and graceful draining. A message is acknowledged only after successful processing; retryable failures are negatively acknowledged under bounded backoff and terminal failures take an explicit path.
requirements.title: Durable consumer framework with explicit acknowledgement

requirements.description: Durable PostgreSQL-backed consumer idempotency keyed by consumer name and event_id, applied in the same database transaction as the handler effect, so at-least-once delivery and lost acknowledgements never produce a duplicate business effect and concurrent duplicate deliveries resolve to exactly one effect.
requirements.title: Consumer idempotency and duplicate protection

requirements.description: Bounded exponential backoff with a maximum delay and a maximum attempt count for both outbox publication and consumer processing, and a deliberate terminal failure strategy (durable dead-letter records and a dead-letter subject) that retains event identity, failure classification, attempt count and sanitized error information without stack traces or secrets, with controlled replay tooling. Poison messages cannot cause an infinite hot loop.
requirements.title: Retry, backoff and terminal failure handling

requirements.description: Tenant authority for an internally produced event comes only from trusted server-side context written into the envelope and outbox, never from an untrusted payload field; consumers establish tenant database scope from the verified envelope and PostgreSQL Row-Level Security remains the final boundary. Forged organization_id, cross-tenant aggregate identifiers, scope confusion and cross-tenant reads or writes fail closed.
requirements.title: Tenant-safe event propagation and isolation

requirements.description: A decoder registry of typed Pydantic event payload models with an explicit envelope schema version and payload version, deterministic handling of unknown event types and unsupported future versions, documented backward-compatible evolution rules and explicit additional-field behaviour. No handler consumes an arbitrary unknown payload as a trusted structure.
requirements.title: Event schema and version compatibility validation

requirements.description: Lifecycle-safe PostgreSQL persistence and query primitives for the event platform tables (outbox, consumer receipts, dead letters) with reversible Alembic migrations, explicit TENANT-OWNED classification, forced Row-Level Security, supporting indexes justified by real claim and lookup query paths, and no import-time connections.
requirements.title: Event persistence and query primitives
